correctness.rationale: For every m >= 1 and all positive distinct radii, periods, and positive nonunit multipliers, K can be chosen so that |w_i| < 1. Lagrange polynomials A,B of degree at most m-1 exist. The field has degree exactly 2m, preserves each circle with strictly positive angular speed, and the reciprocal-cosine integral yields exactly its prescribed least period. The radial logarithmic Poincare derivative equals -4 pi K r_i F'(s_i) w_i / omega_i = log(mu_i), proving hyperbolicity for every selected cycle. Conversely, degree <=2m-1 forces the radial polynomial xP+yQ to vanish identically by circle divisibility, degree count, and evaluation at the origin; nearby circles are then periodic, contradicting isolated hyperbolicity. The standalone numerical verification tests interpolation, polynomial degree, period, multiplier, and nonlinear returns for m <= 5. All infinite quantifiers and the lower bound rest on the written analytic proof, not the code.

originality.rationale: The exact degree 2m for curves of algebraic degree 2m is already supported by Christopher (2001), and general period/stability synthesis by Margalef-Bentabol--Peralta-Salas (2015). Christopher accessible abstract does not assert those data; Theorems 2.1, 4.2 and 5.2 of the inspected 2015 primary full text have different degree/data and full-limit-cycle-set requirements. value.rationale: Polynomial degree under prescribed invariant-cycle geometry, physical periods and transverse return eigenvalues is a natural quantitative inverse problem. Prior algebraic curve synthesis achieves degree matching without the simultaneous numeric temporal constraints, while later full-set realization results impose higher degree. Here a nonrotational cosine modulation breaks radial Floquet-sign rigidity and achieves arbitrary independent multiplier magnitudes and periods at the geometry-forced degree floor. The explicit obstruction identifies why any lower-degree field is nonhyperbolic. This is a complete family-wide theorem, not a small coefficient gain or arbitrary parameter slice; the weaker containment scope and historical risks are fully disclosed.
